technical_and_design_decisions: Migrate the existing Spring XD module implementations into the s-c-s repository with minimal behavioral change, preserving their public module names, properties, and source/sink semantics.

Treat the mail source and mail sink requirements as separate module variants, even though both are named mail, because they represent different streaming roles and may have different configuration and implementation behavior.
Use the target repository's existing build, packaging, dependency-management, coding, and test conventions wherever available.
Target Java 17 or later and the Spring Framework version required by the target s-c-s repository; update deprecated or incompatible APIs only as needed for compilation and tests.
Retain the existing transport and storage libraries for syslog, TCP, GPFDist, HDFS, mail, and MongoDB unless they are incompatible with the target platform.
Add or adapt unit and focused integration tests for each migrated module, including configuration binding and representative message or data transfer behavior.
Include repository-level CI and packaging validation so that all migrated modules can be built and published using the s-c-s build.
Do not introduce new functionality, performance improvements, protocol changes, or broad refactoring beyond what is required to make the modules build and operate in the target repository.
assumptions: The source code, tests, metadata, and relevant documentation for all eight requirements are available in the existing Spring XD repository.
The target s-c-s repository already exists and provides a standard project structure, build system, dependency repositories, and module integration conventions.
One workday represents one developer working day of approximately eight hours; the estimate is effort, not elapsed calendar time.
The developer is responsible for all implementation, testing, documentation, and CI changes, with no parallel development support.
The mail source and mail sink are estimated as separate migrations because the specification assigns them separate source and sink roles.
External systems such as mail servers, HDFS, MongoDB, GPFDist endpoints, TCP peers, and syslog emitters are available for testing or can be represented by local test doubles.
No production deployment, operational infrastructure provisioning, security review, licensing review, or long-term support work is included.
Existing functionality is assumed to be generally correct; the effort includes fixing migration-related defects but not redesigning defective legacy behavior.
Code review feedback is limited to one normal review-and-rework cycle and is covered within the listed activities.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the Spring XD implementations, build descriptors, dependencies, tests, configuration properties, licensing metadata, and the target s-c-s repository conventions; produce a migration checklist for all eight requirements.

activities.activity_name: Target repository and build integration setup
activities.activity_description: Create or update module directories, parent build declarations, dependency management, Java and Spring compatibility settings, packaging metadata, and local build configuration required to host the migrated modules.
Move the syslog source implementation and metadata, adapt package and configuration integration to s-c-s conventions, resolve dependencies, and perform a local build and smoke validation.
Move the mail source implementation, polling and message conversion configuration, metadata, and associated resources; adapt APIs and dependencies and perform a local smoke validation.
Move the TCP source implementation and configuration, preserve connection and message framing behavior, adapt target-repository APIs and dependencies, and perform a local smoke validation.
Move the TCP client source implementation and configuration, preserve client connection and polling behavior, adapt APIs and dependencies, and perform a local smoke validation.
Move the GPFDist sink implementation, protocol-related configuration, metadata, and resources; adapt dependencies and validate representative outbound data transfer.

Move the HDFS dataset sink implementation and configuration, adapt Hadoop/HDFS dependencies and target APIs, preserve dataset-writing behavior, and perform representative local or test-double validation.
Move the mail sink implementation, message composition and delivery configuration, metadata, and resources; adapt APIs and dependencies and validate representative outbound mail generation.
Move the Mongo sink implementation and configuration, adapt MongoDB driver and Spring dependencies, preserve document-write behavior, and perform representative persistence validation.
Port existing tests, add missing configuration and message-flow tests, update mocks and test fixtures for the target framework, and verify source and sink behavior for all migrated modules.
Update module descriptions, configuration/property documentation, usage examples, migration notes, licensing and notices, and repository navigation metadata.
Add or update CI jobs, build profiles, static checks, test execution, artifact packaging, and dependency or compatibility checks for the migrated modules.
Build the complete repository, execute representative source-to-sink pipeline checks using available test doubles or local services, resolve migration defects, and perform final review and cleanup.
